rootCause: The issue text asks for the "Theme" value to be usable to conditionally render react-icons. The value is still the raw next-themes `theme`: undefined on the server/first render and "system" by default, so `theme === "dark"` in TeamMember.tsx is false for a system-dark user and the icon is painted black on a dark background. The mode toggle was hardened (da1a1f7d) but the shared provider was not given a defined default, and the icons named in the issue were not migrated to `resolvedTheme`. The issue was closed on 2024-08-22 without a matching commit; the only later reference (bot comment pointing at PR #2735 / 20f59d0e) is a CI release-gate change that is not in master and has nothing to do with theming.

summary: A read-only dry-run Twilio prune report exists in master (scripts/twilio-resource-prune-report.mjs) driven by a shared policy module that classifies every resource as KEEP / STALE / UNKNOWN with an environment check and an owner check, and the only deletion path (scripts/local/prune-environment-twiml-apps.mjs) deletes nothing but closed pull-request preview TwiML Apps, dry-run by default.
currentBehavior: The claimed fix does not resolve the reported symptom.
resolution: Implement the missing mechanism named in the root cause.
existingTests: test/twilio-resource-prune-policy.test.ts — 31 policy cases (environment check, owner check, keep list, assertPrunable guard); no test exercises a real delete (there is no delete path for workspace-owned resources)
rootCause: PARTIAL, and manual. The report and both checks are in master, but the goal says "Find and remove stale Twilio resources in development, review, and closed-preview environments" and the removal half is only implemented for closed-preview TwiML Apps: the only `.remove()` call in the repo is in prune-environment-twiml-apps.mjs. There is no delete path for a stale messaging service, incoming phone number, or subaccount, and by design a workspace-owned resource can never be STALE (UNKNOWN), so dev/review-owned resources are never removed automatically — that matches the issue's own "do not remove production resources automatically" but leaves "remove in development and review environments" unbuilt. The report is a script against a live Twilio account with live credentials and a live database, so a human must run it and act on the STALE list to confirm the behaviour; the classification logic itself is machine-checked. Also note the candidate PR commit b4046027 is unrelated to this issue (it is a CI ledger-drift gate) — the real work is the 2026-10-19 release commit 91c4409b, which added the report, the policy module and the shared live-environment list.
